target_customer: Developers and teams using coding agents who want lightweight specs as durable context
problem: Coding agents lose context on complex features; OpenSpec provides spec documents that keep humans and agents aligned.
business_model: Open source MIT framework from Fission AI; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, spec-driven development framework for coding agents

founders.name: Tabish Bidiwale
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built core platform and products at Q-CTRL from seed through a 113M USD Series B. Education not on the YC page.

competitors.name: GitHub Spec Kit
competitors.what: Open source spec-driven development toolkit for many coding agents

competitors.name: Kiro (AWS)
competitors.what: Spec-driven IDE, a VS Code fork

technical_complexity.rationale: A CLI and markdown spec workflow is simple to build; value comes from workflow design and adoption.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and copyable, with backed rivals from GitHub and AWS; community and star count are the main assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GitHub and AWS shipped Spec Kit and Kiro in 2025 before the batch; OpenSpec kept growing, with Thoughtworks moving it to Trial in November 2026.

market_need_then: Coding agent adoption in 2025 created a context problem; several spec tools launched at once, which indicates demand.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened

branding.brand_signature: Lightweight planning for coding agents; large GitHub star count
branding.community_and_virality: Discord community, GitHub stars reported at 27k on the YC page and 66.2k on the company site, plus coverage by Thoughtworks Radar and dev blogs.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer awareness through stars and independent coverage, though the name is generic and no brand design material was found.

outcome_analysis: OpenSpec grew rapidly as an open source project, reporting over 265,000 monthly developers and 66.2k stars (company claims), and Thoughtworks placed it in Trial in November 2026. Its risk is monetization and large vendors with competing spec tools. No exit; no verified funding.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists about 500K USD pre-seed in March 2026 with YC and Pioneer Fund, and a Dealroom item says Tekedia Capital invested in June 2026 with no amount; the Dealroom page was not readable (rate limited), so no rounds are recorded. A directory lists a University of Sydney degree for the founder, but the page was not opened, so education is empty. The YC page gave team size blank.
